The evidence explicitly describes a 'cascaded binary merge tree' algorithm that merges sorted splat lists from 'multiple active renderers' into a 'single globally sorted order buffer'. It details the process of packing data from individual renderers and merging them using global scratch buffers and a final global order buffer. This confirms that the method delegates the sorting execution to a global mechanism (the merge tree/global buffers) rather than having each renderer handle sorting independently, which aligns with the claim's description of contrasting with 'per-renderer rendering'.
